title: The infinitesimal-point equivalence sends multiplication to addition
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ a group scheme over $S$, with Lie algebra as in [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation]. Let $\operatorname{infPoints}(G)$ be the kernel of $G(S[\varepsilon])\to G(S)$, using [def-sc-dual-numbers]. The canonical equivalence to $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_S}(e^*\Omega^1_{G/S},\mathcal O_S)$ sends $vw$ to the sum of the images of $v$ and $w$.

source.place: Lemma 33.16.2 proof, square-zero pushout addition; sectionwise arbitrary-base form and group unit-law application

proof.text: For v,w in infPoints G define f:D times_S D to G by multiplying v after the first projection and w after the second. Product projection identities show its diagonal restriction is vw. The reductions of v,w are the identity; the two group unit laws show its first-axis restriction is v and its second-axis restriction is w. Their reductions therefore all equal the unit section.

Apply tangent addition on the diagonal to f with g equal to the unit section. Transported omegaHom respects equality of points by equality induction. Rewrite the three restrictions to obtain toLie(vw)=toLie(v)+toLie(w). The equivalence lieEquiv has exactly toLie as its underlying function.

proof_origin.place: Square-zero addition calculation, applied sectionwise over arbitrary base schemes; group-unit-law and universal-differential glue written by G3
